To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
PAF-induced neutrophylic infiltration and gastric hemorrhage were differentially antagonized by the PAF antagonists Ro24-4738 and CV-3988 in the rat.
PAF-induced neutropenia and gastric hemorrhage are differentially antagonized by two PAF receptor antagonists.
platelet-activating factor (PAF)-antagonist Ro 24-4736 prevents PAF-induced neutrophylic leukocytosis, but not PAF-induced gastric hemorrhage in rats.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new class of drugs, the PAF antagonists, for the treatment of diseases in which PAF is involved.
the effects of platelet activating factors (PAFs) on neutrophils and on gastric hemorrhage in rats.
the role of PAF in the pathogenesis of gastric hemorrhage and neutrophilia.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PAF receptors in neutrophil mobilizing systems are distinct from PAF receptors that mediate gastrointestinal and cardiovascular responses.
PAF antagonists can prevent the PAF-induced hypotension and gastric lesions in the rat.
PAF-induced hypotension, gastric congestion, gastric epithelial sloughing, and neutrophilia are mediated by PAF receptors that are not identical in their pharmacology.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
PAF-induced gastric hemorrhage is not dependent on the neutrophil response.
PAF receptors in neutrophils are different from PAF receptors involved with cardiovascular and gastrointestinal systems.
the PAF-induced neutrophylic infiltration is a result of a direct effect of PAF on the bone marrow.
The main takeaway from our work is that

there are multiple PAF receptor subtypes and that the PAF receptor sub-type involved in neutrophil mobilizing activity is different from the PAF receptor subtype that is involved in cardiovascular and gastrointestinal activity.
there are at least three different types of PAF receptors in rats.
PAF antagonists may be effective in preventing PAF-induced gastrointestinal damage without interfering with PAF-mediated leukocyte mobilization.
